title: Claude-Assisted Smooth C^∞ Counterexample Challenging the 1924 Carathéodory Conjecture
whyItMatters: Proposes an explicit C^∞ convex-body support function with a single index-2 umbilic point—challenging the 102-year-old Carathéodory conjecture—though actively contested against prior published proofs.
summary: On August 19, 2026, Anthropic/Harvard mathematician Levent Alpöge announced on X an explicit family of smooth C^∞ support functions g_k, claiming that g_2 defines a closed, smooth convex surface in ℝ³ with exactly one umbilic point (of index 2)—which would refute the 1924 Carathéodory conjecture in the smooth non-analytic category. Alpöge credited John-Paul Smith and Anthropic’s Claude with checking the explicit construction. Because the result was announced on X without a refereed preprint or Lean formalization and directly conflicts with Guilfoyle & Klingenberg’s 2025 claimed C^{3,α} proof, its status remains contested pending formal verification.
technicalHighlights: Constructs an explicit family of C^∞ support functions g_k whose member g_2 is claimed to yield a smooth convex ovaloid with exactly one umbilic point of index 2.
Explicitly credits Anthropic’s Claude alongside John-Paul Smith for checking the differential-geometric calculations.
Highlights the tension between rapid social-media AI math announcements and classical differential geometry (directly contradicting Guilfoyle & Klingenberg, 2025).
caveats: Indexed candidly as Contested / Partial: announced via X without a peer-reviewed paper or Lean 4 formalization, and directly conflicts with Guilfoyle & Klingenberg’s 2025 claimed proof for C^{3,α} surfaces.

scoreRationale.foundational: If validated, refuting the 102-year-old smooth Carathéodory conjecture would overturn a famous pillar of global differential geometry.
scoreRationale.ripple: Prefigured Alpöge and Claude’s November 2026 Lean Riemann Hypothesis effort and sparked intense scrutiny of smooth umbilic claims.
scoreRationale.verification: Marked low (45) and Contested / Partial: X announcement only, no Lean proof, and conflicts with published 2025 work.
scoreRationale.velocity: Explicit analytical support-function counterexample constructed and checked within roughly a week.
